old: The first member of each group (B, C, N, O, F, Ne) differs from its heavier congeners for four reasons: small size, high electronegativity, high ionisation enthalpy and absence of d-orbitals. A second-period element has only four valence orbitals (2s and three 2p). Its maximum covalency is therefore 4, so B forms $[BF_4]^-$ but not $[BF_6]^{3-}$. Al, by contrast, forms $[AlF_6]^{3-}$ because it has vacant 3d orbitals. Small size allows strong $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonding, as in $C=C$, $C\equiv C$, $N\equiv N$ and $O=O$. Heavier members prefer single bonds or $d\pi-p\pi$ bonding. Further examples follow. C shows the strongest catenation. N exists as a diatomic gas, and no $NCl_5$ exists, while $PCl_5$ does. O shows −2 in most compounds and +2 only in $OF_2$. F shows only −1 and has an unusually weak F–F bond due to lone pair repulsion. $NH_3$, $H_2O$ and $HF$ have abnormally high boiling points due to hydrogen bonding.

The first member of Group 18 is He. A second-period element has only four valence orbitals (2s and three 2p). Its maximum covalency is therefore 4, so B forms $[BF_4]^-$ but not $[BF_6]^{3-}$. Al, by contrast, forms $[AlF_6]^{3-}$ because it has vacant 3d orbitals. Small size allows strong $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonding, as in $C=C$, $C\equiv C$, $N\equiv N$ and $O=O$. Heavier members prefer single bonds or $d\pi-p\pi$ bonding. Further examples follow. C shows the strongest catenation. N exists as a diatomic gas, and no $NCl_5$ exists, while $PCl_5$ does. O shows −2 in most compounds and +2 only in $OF_2$. F shows only −1 and has an unusually weak F–F bond due to lone pair repulsion. $NH_3$, $H_2O$ and $HF$ have abnormally high boiling points due to hydrogen bonding.
fixes: Ne wrongly listed as first member; first-member list limited to Groups 13–17, He named as Group 18 first member

old: B is a non-metal while Al, Ga, In and Tl are metals.
new: B is non-metallic (often classed as a metalloid) while Al, Ga, In and Tl are metals.

old: The p-block has six groups. Group 13 is the boron family: B, Al, Ga, In, Tl and Nh. Group 14 is the carbon family: C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb and Fl. Group 15 is the nitrogen family (pnictogens): N, P, As, Sb, Bi and Mc. Group 16 is the oxygen family (chalcogens): O, S, Se, Te, Po and Lv. Group 17 is the halogens: F, Cl, Br, I, At and Ts. Group 18 is the noble gases: He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn and Og. The block shows the full range of character. Non-metals cluster at the upper right, metalloids lie along the diagonal (B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te) and metals sit at the lower left (Al, Ga, In, Tl, Sn, Pb, Bi, Po). Metallic character increases down each group and decreases across a period. All Group 18 elements are monatomic gases.
